subject: Data Structures & Algorithms in C

projects.title: In-Memory Key-Value Store Database Engine
projects.description: Build an in-memory Key-Value database store (like Redis) in C! Supports `SET key value`, `GET key`, and `DELETE key` operations using separate chaining Hash Maps with string keys and dynamic string values in `O(1)` average time. In this project, you will build Key-Value Store Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Redis-Style Key-Value Stores, Separate Chaining Hash Tables & O(1) Data Retrieval
projects.exampleText: Execute SET, GET, and DELETE commands in Key-Value store
projects.exampleOutput:
--- In-Memory Key-Value Store Database Engine ---
Executed SET, GET, DELETE operations over Hash Map index in O(1) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Hash Table Index**: Compute hash index using DJB2 algorithm.
2. **Operations API**: Implement `set()`, `get()`, and `del()` with dynamic memory allocation.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `kv_store_capstone_demo()`: Solves In-Memory Key-Value Store Database Engine.

projects.title: Command-Line File System Navigator Engine
projects.description: Build a command-line file system directory tree navigator (like UNIX `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `rm`). Model files and directories as an N-ary Tree where each directory node contains a linked list of child directory/file nodes! In this project, you will build File System Navigator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: N-ary Tree Structures, Directory Navigation Algorithms & Shell File System Engines
projects.exampleText: Navigate n-ary tree file system directory hierarchy
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Command-Line File System Navigator Engine ---
Navigated n-ary tree file system directory hierarchy.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **N-ary Tree Nodes**: Each node contains `name`, `is_dir` flag, `parent` pointer, and `children` list.
2. **Directory Commands**: `mkdir` appends child node; `cd` changes current working node.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `filesystem_navigator_demo()`: Solves Command-Line File System Navigator Engine.

projects.title: Expression Calculator Engine (Infix to Postfix & Evaluation)
projects.description: Build a complete mathematical expression calculator. 1) Convert Infix string `(3 + 4) * 5` into Reverse Polish Notation (Postfix) `3 4 + 5 *` using the Shunting-Yard Algorithm; 2) Evaluate Postfix expression using a Stack to compute result `35`! In this project, you will build Expression Calculator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Shunting-Yard Algorithm, Infix-to-Postfix Conversions & Stack Expression Evaluation
projects.exampleText: Evaluate Infix expression (3 + 4) * 5 to output 35
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Expression Calculator Engine ---
Evaluated Infix expression '(3 + 4) * 5' → Postfix '3 4 + 5 *' → Output = 35.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Shunting-Yard Pass**: Convert infix string to postfix tokens using operator precedence stack.
2. **Postfix Evaluation**: Push numbers onto stack; pop operands on operator and push result.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `expression_calculator_demo()`: Solves Expression Calculator Engine.

projects.title: Text Editor Buffer Engine (Gap Buffer / Rope Data Structure)
projects.description: Build a high-performance Text Editor Buffer engine used in text editors like Emacs or Vim. Implements a **Gap Buffer** (a single buffer with a movable cursor gap) that allows `O(1)` text insertions and deletions at the cursor location! In this project, you will build Gap Buffer Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Gap Buffer Data Structures, Text Editor Architectures & O(1) Cursor Insertion/Deletion
projects.exampleText: Execute text insertions and cursor moves inside Gap Buffer
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Text Editor Buffer Engine (Gap Buffer) ---
Executed text insertions and cursor moves inside Gap Buffer in O(1) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Gap Buffer Structure**: Buffer split into `prefix`, `gap`, and `suffix`.
2. **Cursor Motion**: Move gap start/end pointers to shift cursor without full memory copies.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `text_editor_buffer_demo()`: Solves Text Editor Buffer Engine.

projects.title: Student Management System Database Engine
projects.description: Build a complete CLI Student Management System in C. Supports adding, searching, updating, sorting, and deleting student records using dynamic struct arrays and binary search indexing. Persists records to binary disk files! In this project, you will build Student Database System in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic Record Management, Binary Search Indexing & Disk File Persistence
projects.exampleText: Manage student records using dynamic array indexes and binary search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Student Management System Database Engine ---
Managed student records using dynamic array indexes and binary search.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Record Struct**: Store `roll_no`, `name`, `gpa`, and `department`.
2. **Binary Search**: Keep array sorted by `roll_no` to enable `O(log N)` lookup.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `student_db_system_demo()`: Solves Student Management System Database Engine.

projects.title: Undo-Redo Command Engine using Stack Data Structures
projects.description: Build an Undo-Redo action engine used in graphics and word processing applications. Maintains TWO stacks: `UndoStack` and `RedoStack`. Executing a new action pushes onto `UndoStack` and clears `RedoStack`; invoking `UNDO` pops from `UndoStack` onto `RedoStack` in `O(1)` time! In this project, you will build Undo-Redo Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dual Stack Operations, Action History Management & O(1) Undo/Redo State Machine
projects.exampleText: Execute UNDO and REDO command history operations
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Undo-Redo Command Engine ---
Executed UNDO and REDO actions using dual Stack data structures.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Undo Action**: Pop state from `UndoStack` and push onto `RedoStack`.
2. **Redo Action**: Pop state from `RedoStack` and push onto `UndoStack`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `undo_redo_engine_demo()`: Solves Undo-Redo Command Engine.

projects.title: Bank Account Transaction Processing Queue Engine
projects.description: Build a concurrent Bank Account Transaction Processing Engine. Enqueues deposit/withdrawal request structures into a thread-safe Queue and processes transactions in strict FIFO order, ensuring atomic account balance updates! In this project, you will build Transaction Queue Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: FIFO Transaction Processing, Queue Data Structures & Atomic Account Balance Updates
projects.exampleText: Process banking transactions in FIFO queue order
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bank Account Transaction Processing Queue Engine ---
Processed banking transaction queue FIFO order with thread-safe queue.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **FIFO Queue**: Maintain `head` and `tail` pointers for incoming transactions.
2. **Atomic Processing**: Process transactions sequentially; reject invalid withdrawals.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bank_transaction_queue_demo()`: Solves Bank Account Transaction Processing Queue Engine.

projects.title: File Compression Utility Engine using Run-Length Encoding (RLE)
projects.description: Build a command-line file compression utility using Run-Length Encoding (RLE). Compresses consecutive repeated byte sequences into `count + byte` pairs (e.g. `WWWWWWWWWWWWBWWWWWWWWWWWWBBB` → `12W1B12W3B`). Achieves 50% compression ratio on repeated data! In this project, you will build RLE Compression Utility in C.
projects.learningOutcome: File RLE Compression, Byte Run Counting & Decompression Utility Engines
projects.exampleText: Compress file using Run-Length Encoding (RLE)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- File Compression Utility Engine using RLE ---
Compressed 'WWWWWWWWWWWWBWWWWWWWWWWWWBBB' → '12W1B12W3B' (50% compression ratio).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Run Counter**: Count consecutive matching bytes `count`.
2. **RLE Stream**: Output `count` and `byte`; decompress by expanding byte `count` times.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `rle_compression_demo()`: Solves File Compression Utility Engine using RLE.

projects.title: Phone Book Contact Directory Search Engine using Trie
projects.description: Build a real-time Phone Book Contact Directory Search Engine. Uses a Prefix Tree (Trie) to store contact names: typing a prefix like `'John'` instantly returns all auto-complete suggestions `['John Doe', 'Johnny', 'Johnson']` in `O(L)` prefix search time! In this project, you will build Phone Book Trie Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Trie Auto-Complete Search, Contact Directory Prefix Trees & Sub-Millisecond Lookups
projects.exampleText: Search contact auto-complete suggestions via Trie prefix search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Phone Book Contact Directory Search Engine ---
Prefix Auto-Complete for 'John' → ['John Doe', 'Johnny', 'Johnson'].
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Trie Insert**: Insert contact name into 26-child Trie node network.
2. **Prefix DFS**: Traverse prefix `p`; run DFS to collect all leaf words under prefix subtree.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `phonebook_trie_demo()`: Solves Phone Book Contact Directory Search Engine.

projects.title: Maze Solver Pathfinder Engine using BFS & DFS
projects.description: Build a 2D Maze Pathfinder Engine. Compare: 1) **BFS Pathfinding**: Guarantees the SHORTEST path from Start to Exit in `O(R * C)` time; 2) **DFS Pathfinding**: Finds a path using less memory recursion depth! In this project, you will build Maze Pathfinder Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Grid BFS vs DFS Pathfinding, Shortest Path Proofs & Maze Navigation Graphs
projects.exampleText: Find shortest path through 2D maze using BFS and DFS
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maze Solver Pathfinder Engine using BFS & DFS ---
BFS Shortest Path Length = 12 moves | DFS Path Length = 18 moves.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **BFS Queue**: Use Queue for shortest path expansion level by level.
2. **Parent Tracking**: Reconstruct exact path coordinates from Exit to Start.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `maze_pathfinder_demo()`: Solves Maze Solver Pathfinder Engine.

projects.title: Real-Time GPS Route Navigation Engine using Dijkstra & A* Search
projects.description: Build a real-time GPS Navigation Engine for road networks. Implement Dijkstra's algorithm and **A* Heuristic Search** (`f(n) = g(n) + h(n)`) using Euclidean distance heuristic to find the fastest driving route across 10,000 map nodes in milliseconds! In this project, you will build GPS Route Navigation Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: GPS Road Network Graphs, A* Heuristic Search, Dijkstra Shortest Path & Priority Queues
projects.exampleText: Find optimal driving route across road graph using A* Search
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Real-Time GPS Route Navigation Engine (A* Search) ---
Evaluated 45 road nodes; found optimal route in 1.2 ms using A* Heuristic Search.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **A* Heuristic**: `h(n) = sqrt((x_n - x_target)^2 + (y_n - y_target)^2)`.
2. **Min-Heap Priority Queue**: Expand node with lowest `f(n) = g(n) + h(n)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `gps_navigation_demo()`: Solves Real-Time GPS Route Navigation Engine using A* Search.

projects.title: High-Speed File Archiver Compression Engine using Huffman Coding
projects.description: Build a production ZIP-style file compressor utility in C using **Huffman Coding**! 1) Calculate byte frequencies; 2) Build Min-Heap Huffman Tree; 3) Generate variable-length prefix-free bit codes; 4) Compress text files by 40%-60%! In this project, you will build Huffman Archiver Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Huffman Coding Architecture, Variable-Length Prefix Codes, Min-Heap Trees & Bit-Packing
projects.exampleText: Compress text file using Huffman Coding algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- High-Speed File Archiver Compression Engine (Huffman Coding) ---
Compressed text file from 100 KB to 58 KB (42% Huffman Compression Ratio).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Huffman Tree**: Build binary tree bottom-up from Min-Heap frequency nodes.
2. **Bit Stream Packing**: Pack variable bit codes into 8-bit output file stream.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `huffman_archiver_demo()`: Solves High-Speed File Archiver Compression Engine.

projects.title: LRU & LFU Multi-Tier Cache Memory Management System
projects.description: Build a multi-tier Cache Engine combining LRU (Least Recently Used via Doubly Linked List + Hash Map) and LFU (Least Frequently Used via Frequency Buckets). Achieves 92%+ hit ratio in sub-microsecond `O(1)` time! In this project, you will build Multi-Tier Cache Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: LRU/LFU Cache Architecture, Doubly Linked Lists, Hash Maps & Sub-Microsecond O(1) Evictions
projects.exampleText: Execute O(1) cache get/put operations with LRU/LFU evictions
projects.exampleOutput:
--- LRU & LFU Multi-Tier Cache Memory Management System ---
Cache Hit Ratio: 92.4% (Evicted least recently/frequently used items in O(1) time).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **LRU Doubly Linked List**: Move accessed node to head; evict tail node when capacity reached.
2. **Hash Map Index**: Direct `O(1)` pointer lookup to cache nodes.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lru_lfu_cache_demo()`: Solves LRU & LFU Multi-Tier Cache Memory Management System.

projects.title: In-Memory B-Tree Database Indexing Engine
projects.description: Build a B-Tree Database Indexing Engine (used in MySQL / SQLite database indices). Implements B-Tree node splitting, key search, insertion, and deletion in `O(log_t N)` disk/memory accesses! In this project, you will build B-Tree Indexing Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: B-Tree Database Indexing, Node Splitting Mechanics & O(log_t N) Disk/Memory Searches
projects.exampleText: Index 1,000,000 database record keys using B-Tree
projects.exampleOutput:
--- In-Memory B-Tree Database Indexing Engine ---
Searched 1,000,000 database record keys in O(log_t N) disk/memory accesses.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **B-Tree Node Split**: Split full node (2t-1 keys) into two nodes with t-1 keys.
2. **Multi-Way Search**: Traverse child pointer where key falls between node key range.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `btree_indexing_demo()`: Solves In-Memory B-Tree Database Indexing Engine.

projects.title: Network Packet Router Simulation Engine using Max-Flow Min-Cut
projects.description: Simulate a Telecommunications Network Packet Router. Model routers as graph nodes and network fiber cables as directed edges with bandwidth capacities. Use Dinic's Max-Flow algorithm to calculate maximum throughput (450 Mbps) and identify bottleneck Min-Cut links! In this project, you will build Packet Router Simulation Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Network Max-Flow Simulations, Dinic Algorithm, Bottleneck Min-Cut Link Audits
projects.exampleText: Calculate maximum network throughput and min-cut bottleneck links
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Network Packet Router Simulation Engine (Max-Flow Min-Cut) ---
Max Network Bandwidth Throughput = 450 Mbps (Identified bottleneck min-cut links).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Max-Flow Network**: Compute maximum flow from S to T using Dinic level graph.
2. **Min-Cut Identification**: Trace residual network reachability to identify bottleneck links.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `packet_router_flow_demo()`: Solves Network Packet Router Simulation Engine.

projects.title: Real-Time Stock Order Book Engine using Heap & Hash Maps
projects.description: Build a financial Stock Exchange Order Book Engine (like NASDAQ). Maintains a **Buy Max-Heap** (highest bid price first) and **Sell Min-Heap** (lowest ask price first). Matches orders at sub-microsecond speed when `bid >= ask`! In this project, you will build Stock Order Book Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Financial Matching Engine Architecture, Buy Max-Heap / Sell Min-Heap & Sub-Microsecond Matching
projects.exampleText: Match buy and sell stock orders at sub-microsecond speed
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Real-Time Stock Order Book Engine (Heap & Hash Map) ---
Matched Buy Max-Heap and Sell Min-Heap orders at sub-microsecond latency.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Priority Heap**: Max-Heap for Bids; Min-Heap for Asks.
2. **Order Matching Loop**: While `bids.top() >= asks.top()`, execute transaction trade.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stock_order_book_demo()`: Solves Real-Time Stock Order Book Engine.

projects.title: Plagiarism Detection Engine using Rabin-Karp & KMP Pattern Matching
projects.description: Build a Document Plagiarism Detection Engine. Scans 1,000 student essay documents against a reference database using **Rabin-Karp Rolling Hash** for fast multi-pattern matching and **KMP** for exact verification! Returns similarity percentage report. In this project, you will build Plagiarism Detection Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Plagiarism Detection Algorithms, Rabin-Karp Rolling Hashes & KMP Exact Matching
projects.exampleText: Detect document plagiarism matches via Rabin-Karp and KMP
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Plagiarism Detection Engine (Rabin-Karp & KMP) ---
Plagiarism Similarity Score: 78.4% match detected across 1,000 document samples.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Rolling Hash Sweep**: Scan N-gram rolling hashes across essay documents.
2. **KMP Verification**: Verify matching hash hits using KMP pattern matcher.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `plagiarism_checker_demo()`: Solves Plagiarism Detection Engine.

projects.title: Social Network Graph Analytics Engine (SCC & Shortest Path)
projects.description: Build a Social Network Graph Analytics Engine (like LinkedIn/Facebook). Computes: 1) **6 Degrees of Separation** via BFS; 2) **Strongly Connected User Communities** via Tarjan's SCC algorithm; 3) **Influencer Recommendations** via In-Degree centrality! In this project, you will build Social Network Graph Analytics Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Social Network Graph Mining, 6 Degrees Separation BFS & Tarjan's Community SCCs
projects.exampleText: Calculate 6 degrees of separation and strongly connected user communities
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Social Network Graph Analytics Engine ---
Identified 4 strongly connected user communities and calculated 6 degrees of separation.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Shortest Distance BFS**: Calculate shortest degree path between user nodes.
2. **Tarjan SCC**: Extract strongly connected user communities.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `social_graph_analytics_demo()`: Solves Social Network Graph Analytics Engine.

projects.title: Task Scheduler & Load Balancer Engine using Min-Priority Queue
projects.description: Build a Cloud Server Task Scheduler & Load Balancer Engine. Schedules 10,000 incoming tasks across N server nodes by dispatching tasks to the server with MINIMUM current workload using a Min-Heap Priority Queue! In this project, you will build Task Scheduler Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Cloud Load Balancing Algorithms, Min-Heap Priority Queues & Workload Distribution
projects.exampleText: Balance incoming tasks across server nodes using Min-Heap
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Task Scheduler & Load Balancer Engine ---
Balanced 10,000 incoming tasks across 8 server nodes with min-heap priority queue.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Min-Heap Server Queue**: Min-Heap orders servers by `current_workload`.
2. **Task Dispatch**: Extract minimum workload server, assign task, and re-insert into heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `task_scheduler_load_balancer_demo()`: Solves Task Scheduler & Load Balancer Engine.

projects.title: Dynamic Programming Spell Checker & Auto-Correct System
projects.description: Build a real-time Spell Checker & Auto-Correct System. Reads misspelled input words (e.g. `'graffe'`), queries a 100,000-word dictionary, and calculates 2D Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance) to output top 3 auto-correct replacements in `O(N * M)` time! In this project, you will build Spell Checker System in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Auto-Correct Architectures, Levenshtein Edit Distance 2D DP & Dictionary Candidate Searches
projects.exampleText: Suggest auto-correct replacements for misspelled words via 2D Edit Distance
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dynamic Programming Spell Checker & Auto-Correct System ---
Suggested auto-correct replacements for 'graffe' → ['giraffe' (dist 1), 'graft' (dist 2)].
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Edit Distance DP**: Calculate `min_distance(word, dict_word)` for dictionary words.
2. **Candidate Filter**: Sort dictionary words by edit distance and pick top 3 minimums.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `spell_checker_autocorrect_demo()`: Solves Dynamic Programming Spell Checker & Auto-Correct System.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Telemetry Database Engine
projects.description: Build an industrial-grade telemetry database engine managing 10,000,000 telemetry records per second directly inside memory-mapped shared RAM buffers (`mmap`) with zero-copy binary file indexing! In this project, you will build Telemetry Database Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped Database Engine, 10M Stream Telemetry Records & Zero-Copy Indexing
projects.exampleText: Manage 10M telemetry database records/sec in memory-mapped shared RAM
projects.exampleOutput:
--- High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Telemetry Database Engine ---
Managed 10,000,000 telemetry database records per second in memory-mapped shared RAM.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **mmap Database File**: Memory-map 10 GB binary database file into RAM virtual address space.
2. **Zero-Copy Indexing**: Execute binary search directly over memory-mapped record offsets.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stream_db_engine_demo()`: Implements High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Telemetry Database Engine.

projects.title: Multi-Threaded Distributed Log Processor Kernel
projects.description: High-speed log analytics engines process 50 GB log files across 16 worker threads using Lock-Free Ring Buffers to parse, filter, and summarize server log entries in real-time. In this project, you will build Distributed Log Processor Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multi-Threaded Log Processing, Lock-Free Ring Buffers & 50 GB File Analytics
projects.exampleText: Process 50 GB log files across 16 worker threads via lock-free ring buffers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Multi-Threaded Distributed Log Processor Kernel ---
Processed 50 GB log files across 16 worker threads using lock-free ring buffers.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Ring Buffer Distribution**: Dispatch log lines into lock-free worker ring buffers.
2. **Parallel Regex Parsing**: Worker threads parse log entries concurrently without mutex locks.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `multi_threaded_log_processor_demo()`: Solves Multi-Threaded Distributed Log Processor Kernel.

projects.title: Parallel SIMD-Accelerated Matrix Graph Engine
projects.description: High-performance graph compute engines accelerate adjacency matrix BFS sweeps using 256-bit AVX2 SIMD vector instructions, evaluating 8 graph node transitions concurrently in 1 CPU instruction pass! In this project, you will build SIMD Matrix Graph Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SIMD AVX2 Graph Matrix Computations, 256-Bit Vector Traversals & Hardware Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Evaluate 8 graph BFS matrix transitions in 256-bit AVX2 vector registers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel SIMD-Accelerated Matrix Graph Engine ---
Evaluated 8 graph BFS matrix transitions concurrently in 256-bit AVX2 vector registers.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Vector Register Adjacency**: Load 8 node adjacency mask vectors into AVX2 registers.
2. **SIMD Vector Bitwise OR**: Execute parallel BFS level expansions in 1 clock cycle.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `simd_graph_engine_demo()`: Solves SIMD Matrix Graph Engine.

projects.title: Lock-Free Parallel Task Scheduling System Kernel
projects.description: High-concurrency cloud operating systems schedule 500,000 parallel CPU tasks using atomic Compare-And-Swap (`CAS`) work-stealing task queues without mutex lock overhead. In this project, you will build Lock-Free Task Scheduling Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Lock-Free Task Scheduling Kernels, Atomic CAS Work-Stealing Queues & 500K Task Engine
projects.exampleText: Schedule 500K parallel tasks using atomic CAS work-stealing queues
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Lock-Free Parallel Task Scheduling System Kernel ---
Scheduled 500,000 parallel CPU tasks using atomic CAS work-stealing queues.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Atomic CAS Work Queue**: Manage task queues using atomic CAS pointer updates.
2. **Multi-Thread Workers**: Worker threads steal sub-tasks from worker queues without locks.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lockfree_task_scheduler_demo()`: Solves Lock-Free Parallel Task Scheduling System Kernel.
